items.title: Oxford lets OpenAI train its AI models on Bodleian Library
items.excerpt: Oxford University will let OpenAI train its models on Bodleian Library collections, as staff voice concerns over reputational risk of partnering with ChatGPT's maker. New library/archive AI-training deal (distinct from the Japan used-books and BookPact stories).

items.title: If AI imagines before we do, what is left for illustrators?
items.excerpt: Illustrator Daniela Frongia on publishers using generative AI to produce early cover and design ideas before briefing illustrators, and what that does to the illustrator's role. Cover/illustration angle.

items.title: Apex CoVantage to Launch eden, an AI-Powered Editorial Engine for Publishing, at Frankfurt Book Fair
items.excerpt: Apex CoVantage will launch eden, an AI editorial engine for book and academic publishing, at Frankfurt on Oct 7: subject-aware error detection and equation checking, with copyeditors accepting 80-90% of suggestions and passes running about 3x faster. OFF-LIST press release (concrete Frankfurt exhibitor launch, no on-list coverage found).

items.title: Google's New AI Voice Model Copies a Voice From 30 Seconds - Voice Over Talent Industry News
items.excerpt: Google's new Gemini 3.8 speech models can clone a voice from a 30-second sample, but only after the voice owner records spoken consent. What it means for narrators and voice talent. OFF-LIST (narration-voices angle; Gemini TTS may also surface in other sections).

items.title: 가상융합산업허브 입주 결실…AI·글로벌 음향 결합 오디오북 시장 개척
items.excerpt: Post-production studio Soundgrab and AI voice firm Voicegrab launch a 'hybrid cinema audiobook' solution that combines film-grade sound design with AI voices, aimed at the global audiobook market. Production-side AI narration (Korean). OFF-LIST.

items.title: AI가 쓴 소설 가려내기, 문학 경험보다 AI 사용 경험이 도움 - 플래텀
items.excerpt: Study: readers who had used AI were better at telling AI-written fiction from human fiction than well-read literature fans, but overall participants guessed the author at or below chance. OFF-LIST (Korean).

items.title: AI의 빠른 ‘정답’ vs 인간의 ‘망설임’···작가들이 말하는 ‘AI가 대체 못 할 문학’
items.excerpt: Korean publishing events this year have asked what generative AI means for writers; novelists and poets describe the 'hesitation' and inner life they think AI can't replace in literature. Feature/essay. OFF-LIST (Korean).

items.title: 유페이퍼발 'AI 전자책' 도배 사태 일단락…리디 "확인 후 판매 중단"
items.excerpt: A flood of AI-generated ebooks distributed through self-publishing platform Upaper surfaced en masse on Ridi; Ridi says it will verify and pull them from sale. AI-slop ebook flood (ebook platform angle, distinct from the 09-24 webnovel story). OFF-LIST (Korean).

items.title: 태안군, AI전자출판 청년 창업가 11명 양성
items.excerpt: Taean County trained 11 young founders to produce and sell their own ebooks using AI tools as an 'AI e-publishing' startup program. Local, low priority. OFF-LIST (Korean).

items.title: 멘탯-제이펍, 출판 콘텐츠 AI 활용 정산 체계 구축 맞손
items.excerpt: Book licensing platform Mentat signs an AI licensing deal with IT publisher J-Pub, supplying about 100 technical titles for AI training and citation with a usage-based settlement system. Korean AI licensing deal. OFF-LIST.

items.title: 스위트북, 인공지능(AI) 동화책 플랫폼 ‘AI스토리교실’ 전면 개편 - 매일경제
items.excerpt: Sweetbook overhauls its 'AI Story Classroom' children's picture-book platform: conversational co-creation and more consistent cover and interior illustrations. AI children's book product. OFF-LIST (Korean).

items.title: Straive and Imagetwin partner to bring AI-powered image integrity checks to scientific publishing - StartUp Beat
items.excerpt: Straive and Imagetwin partner to add AI image-integrity checks to scientific publishing workflows as synthetic and manipulated figures get harder to catch. Scholarly publishing tooling. OFF-LIST.

items.title: [단독] ‘AI 직격타’ 논픽션 불황에…교양 전문 출판사, 문학서 활로 모색
items.excerpt: With nonfiction/general-interest sales hit hard by AI answer engines, Korean trade-nonfiction publishers are moving into literary fiction. Market effect of AI on publishing. OFF-LIST (Korean).

items.title: Anthropic settlement increases time to handle disputes | Jane Friedman
items.excerpt: Because of the number of errors in Anthropic settlement claims, rights holders now get 60 days instead of 30 to respond to disputes. Copyright admin update; low priority given heavy copyright coverage.

items.title: ‘They’re likely to get squeezed’: AI slop books are flooding online marketplaces—and it’s coming at the expense of paychecks for human authors | Fortune
items.excerpt: A Stony Brook-led study of 14,419 self-published genre-fiction books on Amazon found thousands with large shares of AI-generated prose; sales volume rose 19x while revenue per book fell, squeezing human authors. OFF-LIST.

items.title: I lost my $2m book deal because people mistook my African dialect for AI
items.excerpt: Jerry Falade, whose $2m debut deal was pulled over AI suspicions, argues that Yoruba storytelling rhythms were mistaken for AI prose. First-person follow-up to an August story. Authorship-accusation angle: push down given Orelien coverage. OFF-LIST.

items.title: Publishers sound alarm over AI-generated textbooks
items.excerpt: Kenyan publishers warn that authors are using AI to generate textbook and learning material, and are training editors to spot it and tightening editorial checks. Textbook/edtech angle. OFF-LIST.
